newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper closes up sharply as funds cover.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper closes up sharply as funds cover.

text.p: COMEX copper ended sharply higher Friday on heavy fund shortcovering, aided by strength in the other base metals, particularly zinc and nickel.

The funds were believed to have amassed short positions over the last month forcing the active September contract to fall from a high of 123.60 cents a lb on June 20 to a low of 104.00 cents on July 9.
The September contract settled at 111.45 cents, up 3.65 cents, while the spot month ended 4.10 cents higher at 114.00 cents.
"The funds have been short all month," said David Rinehimer, director of futures research at Smith Barney. "It feels like an overdue correction in a bear market."

The market took its cue from the zinc and nickel markets in London, he said. The zinc market is currently in the throes of a squeeze in which prices are lodged at seven-year highs. Nickel is at its highest price in a month on strike fears at Falconbridge's Sudbury mine.

Other brokers attributed the buying spree to nothing more than technicals. "We triggered some buy stops above 109.50-110.00 cents (in September)," one said. "It was all short-covering. I didn't see any new positions taken today."
On the fundamental side, the market remains quiet. London Metal Exchange warehouse stocks increased another 5,325 tonnes, to 210,225 tonnes, the highest level since March 3.

In the last five weeks, LME stocks have increased 88,675 tonnes. Many physical dealers attribute part of the increase to arbitrage shipments from COMEX warehouses, whose stocks have declined 21,697 tonnes in the same time frame.

But consumers claim the LME stock increase is indicative of poor demand in the U.S. "It's the summer," said one brass mill executive. "Demand has been weak. If consumers needed copper, we'd be buying it. You wouldn't be seeing these terminal market games between warehouses."
The LME cash price was trading at as much as 6.50 cents over the COMEX spot price last week. Friday, COMEX spot closed at a 3.80-cent premium to LME cash.
((Derek J. Caney, New York Commodity Desk, 212-859-1640))
